project_metadata.job_description:
Wordpress site hosted with WP Engine has slow page load. Seeking developer to diagnose and fix the front-end performance issue.

Scope
- Diagnose root cause of slow page load
- Fix identified issues (assets, scripts, plugins, page builder elements — whatever the diagnosis shows)
- Verify improvement with before/after performance data
- Brief written summary of cause and fix

Requirements
- Proven experience fixing WordPress site speed issues (not just plugin installation)
- Comfortable with WP Engine hosting environment
- Able to read and act on tools like WebPageTest, GTmetrix, Lighthouse

The problem went beyond the fake admin users we found last night. I also discovered a hidden admin account embedded in the database, with around 470 casino spam pages published through it. Code planted in one of your plugins was concealing everything and interfering with the site's caching, which explains why visitors were experiencing page-load times of 15+ seconds.

The cleanup is now complete. It took About 7 hours all in today:
\- Deleted the hidden admin account along with all ~470 spam pages
\- Replaced the compromised plugin with a clean official copy
\- Performed a fresh installation of WordPress itself
\- Coordinated with WP Engine to reset the site's credentials and keys, and requested a full platform-level malware scan as independent confirmation
\- Configured Wordfence as a security scanner so it will notify us if anything suspicious occurs again

The outcome is that pages load in under 2 seconds rather than 16. I'll continue watching the site for the next couple of days to verify that it remains clean.

I need a few actions from you:
1\. The security reset signed everyone out of WordPress. Set a new password when you log back in, and ask every other admin to do likewise
2\. As an additional precaution, change your WP Engine password as well
3\. Grant me access to your Google Search Console so I can remove the spam pages from Google before they damage your rankings. Go to Settings > Users and permissions > Add user > Full access and use this email: [EMAIL_004]
4\. Submit a quick test through the contact form and verify that its email arrives, confirming that your leads still flow correctly after these changes

The remaining items on my list are:
\- Complete the Search Console cleanup after access is granted
\- Update the outdated plugins, which are probably how the attackers originally gained access
\- Provide WP Engine's scan results once they are returned

I'm happy to address any questions, and if you want one for your records, I can also provide a proper written report.
